name: Renal perfusion pressure above which renin release plateaus
citation: van Ochten M, El Fathi W, Bovee EME, Spaanderman MEA, Hooijmans CR, van Drongelen J. The renal baroreflex: a systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy and hypertensive animals. Physiol Rep 2025;13:e70547.
notes: Dose-response meta-analysis: renin falls LINEARLY with rising renal pressure below the threshold and PLATEAUS above it. Threshold 93 +/- 2 mmHg. NOTE this coincides with CV.MAP.SETPOINT = 93.0 to within the reported SD, which means the model's operating point sits AT the threshold and the response is rectified, not symmetric. In hypertensive animals slope is diminished, threshold comparable, plateau slightly lower. Risk of bias reported as high in most included studies.

name: Fractional renin suppression per fractional rise in renal perfusion pressure
citation: Schweda F et al. Blood pressure-dependent inhibition of renin secretion requires A1 adenosine receptors. Hypertension 2006;47:1-7. AND Hofbauer KG et al. Relationship between perfusion pressure and renin release in the isolated rat kidney. Pflugers Arch 1975.
notes: DERIVED, not reported. Schweda isolated perfused mouse kidney from 90 mmHg baseline: 65 mmHg -> 1.4x, 40 mmHg -> 3.6x, 115 mmHg -> 0.64x, 140 mmHg -> 0.40x. Local log-slopes give g = 1.25 (down 25), 2.38 (down 50), 1.66 (up 25), 1.70 (up 50). Taking 1.5 as the near-operating-point value; range covers 1.25-2.38. CONFLICT TO RESOLVE: this isolated prep shows a STEEPER response upward than the in vivo meta-analysis (RAAS.RENIN.PRESSURE_THRESHOLD), which reports a plateau above 93. Isolated kidney lacks neural and systemic input. Hofbauer independently reports inverse dependence over 50-150 mmHg, steepest 90->70, measurable within 1 min and maximal at 5 min. NO human slope available: pressor-dependent renin release in humans is confounded by sympathetic reflex (Jordan et al. Hypertension 1997;30:1068).

name: Log-log slope of plasma aldosterone against plasma renin activity
citation: Wilkins/Oparil-era arterial and venous angiotensin II study, PMID 773568. Cross-checked against Oelkers W et al. and Hollenberg sodium-modulation series (PMID 7026131).
notes: DERIVED. Posture/volume stimulus produced a 5-fold aldosterone rise (5.6 -> 32.0 ng/100 mL) against a 20-fold PRA rise (0.6 -> 13.1 ng/mL/h). log(5)/log(20) = 0.537. The relationship is strongly COMPRESSIVE - a linear gain is wrong. STATE DEPENDENCE, not yet captured: the aldosterone-AngII slope is significantly steeper on low sodium intake than high (PMID 7026131), so this is not a constant. Also TIME dependence: Hall et al. Circ Res 1976;39:788 report the acute aldosterone rise to AngII infusion is markedly attenuated after the first 24 h.

name: Increment in fractional distal sodium reabsorption per unit normalised aldosterone
citation: Yokota N et al. Sodium excretion and atrial natriuretic peptide levels during mineralocorticoid administration: a mechanism for the escape from hyperaldosteronism. PMID 2966064.
notes: WEAKEST ENTRY IN THIS BLOCK - tier C, derived through an assumption I could not source. Fludrocortisone 0.3-0.5 mg/day, sodium intake 180 +/- 2 mEq/day, n=4 healthy males: urinary sodium excretion fell 27 percent acutely = 48.6 mEq/day retained. Against the model's filtered load of 25200 mEq/day that is dFR = 0.00193. But fludrocortisone at that dose is SUPRAphysiological; converting to a per-unit-normalised-aldosterone gain requires assuming a dose equivalence (3-5x normal) that I did not find published. Range 0.00039-0.00064 spans 3x-5x. FIND A DIRECT DOSE-RESPONSE BEFORE TRUSTING THIS.

name: Time constant of escape from the sodium-retaining effect of aldosterone
citation: Kelly TM, Nelson DH. Sodium excretion and atrial natriuretic peptide levels during mineralocorticoid administration. Endocr Res 1987;13(4):363-383. PMID 2966064. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 2026-08-21 - previously and wrongly cited as Yokota N et al. Corroborated: Knox FG et al. Kidney Int 1980;17:263-276; Wang XY et al. J Clin Invest 2001;108:215.
notes: SPECIES FIELD CORRECTED 2026-08-21: previously read 'human; dog; rat', which is cross-species pooling in a single row and is prohibited by validation/pooling.md - a dog value averaged with a human one describes no organism. The primary observation is HUMAN, n=4 (Kelly and Nelson 1987); the dog and rat papers are corroboration and belong in the citation text, not the species field. TIER LOWERED A -> B: n=4 single study is small-n, which is an ADR 0004-shaped weakness and nothing to do with species. doi previously pointed at the Wang paper rather than at PMID 2966064. Urinary sodium excretion returned to baseline in an average of 5 days despite continued fludrocortisone. This is MULTIPLY REPLICATED and it is the reason primary aldosteronism does not produce oedema. MECHANISM IS PARTLY ALREADY IN THE MODEL: escape is driven by pressure natriuresis (present), plus NCC downregulation (absent) and ANP (absent - ANP roughly doubled, 91.7 -> 179.7 pg/mL, in the same study). CONSEQUENCE FOR IPE: if Raas.jl omits escape, aldosterone exerts a permanent sodium-retaining effect that does not exist in vivo, and RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE will appear to need recalibration when it does not.

name: Effective time constant of the circulating angiotensin arm
citation: Busse LW et al. Angiotensin II. PMC6050881 (AngII plasma half-life). Hofbauer KG et al. Pflugers Arch 1975 (renin response kinetics). Skinner SL et al. Control of renin secretion. Circ Res 1964;15:64.
notes: STRUCTURAL POINT: plasma AngII half-life is under 1 minute, so AngII itself is nearly instantaneous on this model's day time base. The rate-limiting step is RENIN, not AngII - renin release is measurable within 60 s and maximal at about 5 min. So the effective lag of the whole arm is renin-limited. Use 5 min; the distinction matters if the arm is ever partitioned per ADR 0003.

name: Fractional rise in total peripheral resistance per unit normalised angiotensin II
notes: DELIBERATELY LEFT BLANK. Human infusion data are abundant but give MAP, not TPR, and the two differ because AngII lowers cardiac output while raising pressure: Charles CJ et al. Biosci Rep 2018 (conscious sheep, 3-48 ng/kg/min) report MAP rising under 10 mmHg at low dose to 23 mmHg at the highest WITH heart rate and cardiac output falling progressively. Townsend RR, DiPette DJ. Am J Physiol 1993;265:E362 report ~15 ng/kg/min raising BP 20/15 mmHg in normotensive men. PMID 7986470 report 2 ng/kg/min as minimally pressor, ~3.3 mmHg. Extracting a TPR gain requires the CO fall, which in IPE should EMERGE from the venous-return path rather than be imposed - so this parameter may not be a free parameter at all. Also sodium-status dependent, in the OPPOSITE direction to the adrenal response: the MAP-AngII slope is steeper on HIGH sodium while the aldosterone-AngII slope is steeper on LOW sodium (PMID 7026131). Resolve the CO question before entering a value.
